tierReason: One cycle from the MVP epic; adds reminder tables, push-token registration and API endpoints

decisions.decision: #10: any project member may add, edit or delete reminders
decisions.why: Matches task editing permissions; mockup assumption 1, user did not object

decisions.decision: #10: at most 5 reminders per task, 20 recipients
decisions.why: Mockup assumption; keeps the 64-pending iOS local notification cap safe

decisions.decision: #10: occurrences scheduled locally 14 days ahead, server push only wakes phones and catches missed ones
decisions.why: Decision 5; works offline and within iOS limits

decisions.decision: #10: monthly repeat uses start day, falling back to the month's last day
#10: reuse expo-notifications and expo-server-sdk; write a small occurrence calculator instead of rrule
decisions.why: Official libs cover push; our 4 repeat rules don't justify rrule plus Luxon

decisions.decision: #10: remote push is off until EAS projectId and token are configured
decisions.why: Local reminders still work, so the feature isn't blocked on the user's Apple setup

decisions.decision: #10: local notifications only, no server push, token or tick work
decisions.why: User has no paid Apple Developer account and wants free notifications (2026-11-18)

decisions.decision: #10: option B — local notifications plus Expo push in Expo Go, sent only by the tick to out-of-date phones
decisions.why: User chose B on 2026-11-18; free, and no duplicate notifications

questions.question: #10: Confirm the mockup assumptions (any member edits reminders; max 5; default time due date 9:00; permission asked on first save; done stops reminders, no snooze)?
#10: Remote push needs an EAS project id and Apple push key (paid Apple Developer account). Do you have one, or should #10 ship with local reminders only and remote push disabled until set up?
questions.answer: No paid Apple account; go with free notifications

serviceActions: Create an EAS project (eas init) and upload an APNs key via eas credentials, then put the projectId in apps/mobile/app.json; optionally create an Expo access token and set EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN on Render
In apps/mobile run npx eas init (free Expo account) and commit extra.eas.projectId in app.json, so phones can get Expo push tokens

findings.text: apps/api/src/tasks/routes.ts:211-216 + apps/mobile/src/tasks/syncCycle.ts:166-174: token lastSyncedAt is stamped on the task-list fetch, before the phone fetches reminders; if /reminders then fails, the server thinks the phone is current and catchUp.ts:112 skips the push, while the phone never scheduled it - reminder silently lost. Stamp only when the reminders fetch succeeds.

apps/api/src/push/catchUp.ts:62-82: each tick loads all non-done reminders with token-holding recipients and all their Nhac kem comments, unbounded; filter by due window in SQL or cap comments per task.
apps/api/src/push/catchUp.ts:121-141: claim row inserted before send; a send failure is only logged, so a transient Expo outage loses that occurrence's push for good.
apps/api/src/reminders/routes.ts:365-393: project reminders list is unpaged and loads every Nhac kem comment then trims to 3 in memory.
apps/api/src/push/catchUp.ts:48-58: overlapping ticks can read the same lastTickAt; duplicates are prevented by the ReminderPushSent claim (note only).

apps/mobile/src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx registerSignOutCleanup has a single slot; ProjectsProvider overwrites TasksProvider's cleanup so the task/reminder caches may not be cleared on sign-out (existing bug, found during Build).

catchUp.ts ~140-150 + sender.ts createExpoSender: the Expo sender swallows chunk failures so the claim-release never runs; when it does throw, lastTickAt still advances so no retry; the 'next tick retries' comment is false.
me/routes.ts ~75-80: moving a token to another user keeps its DeviceProjectSync rows, so the new owner can look synced from the previous owner's fetch and miss a push.
me/routes.ts: per-user token cap judges newest by createdAt, not refreshed on re-register/move, so the just-registered token can be deleted.
catchUp.ts sendDue: unbounded scan each tick (same as finding 2).
catchUp.ts: a crash between claiming and sending loses those pushes (accepted at-most-once trade-off).

testHandoff.steps: Run npm run dev:phone from this branch checkout (after db:deploy on the dev DB), open in Expo Go on the iPhone, sign in, open a task. 1) Tap ＋ Thêm, save a reminder 2 minutes ahead: the explanation sheet, then the iOS prompt (Tiếp tục). 2) Lock the phone, airplane mode on: the notification shows at that time with task title, due/project line and Nhắc kèm comments; tap it: the task opens. 3) Compare the Nhắc nhở section and form with mockup screens 1a-1d, 2a-2d, 4c, 4d (5 reminders -> Tối đa 5; done task -> greyed rows; denied permission -> Mở Cài đặt notice; past one-off and no recipients -> errors, Lưu disabled; offline add -> Chờ lưu then syncs; dark mode, English, VoiceOver names). Expected: all match the mockup, selections highlighted with no ticks.

testHandoff.what: #10 Expo push in Expo Go (R14, R20)
testHandoff.steps: After npx eas init has put extra.eas.projectId in apps/mobile/app.json and cron-job.org calls /internal/tick: on phone A (Lan) sign in and allow notifications, then close the app. On phone B (Huy) add a reminder for Lan 6 minutes ahead on a shared task. Expected: Lan's phone shows the notification within one tick (<=5 min late) without opening the app, and only once. If nothing arrives, Expo Go on SDK 58 may not support push: tell Claude, and #10 keeps local notifications only.
